specification.problem: Reconstruct the abstract's scope: review Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) adders and multipliers, extend them to modular, non-modular, and signed-integer arithmetic, and use the transform domain for weighted averages and inner products of data vectors.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of QFT-based arithmetic primitives (adder, weighted sum, inner product) for a small finite instance with N = 2^n; no full circuit, multiplier, signed-integer encoding, or experimental details are reconstructed.

equations.label: QFT action on a basis state
equations.description: Standard definition of the quantum Fourier transform on a computational basis state.
equations.justification: Standard textbook definition of the QFT; not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Phase-encoded addition in transform domain
equations.latex: |k\rangle\mapsto e^{2\pi i ak/N}|k\rangle \Rightarrow \mathrm{QFT}^{\dagger}\left(e^{2\pi i ak/N}\right)\mathrm{QFT}|x\rangle=|x+a \bmod N\rangle
equations.description: Standard Fourier-domain adder identity underlying QFT-based addition modulo N.
equations.justification: Standard identity behind QFT adders; the abstract mentions QFT adders but not this formula.
assumptions: Phase rotations are applied to the Fourier-transformed register

equations.label: Weighted average of inputs
equations.description: Classical weighted average that the abstract says is computed in the transform domain.
equations.abstract_quote: a quantum method to compute the weighted average of a series of inputs in the transform domain
equations.justification: The abstract names the weighted average target; the explicit formula is the standard definition and is inferred.

equations.label: Inner product of data vectors
equations.description: Inner product computed by the controlled weighted sum circuit, per the abstract's interpretation.
equations.abstract_quote: the controlled weighted sum, can be interpreted as a circuit to compute the inner product of two data vectors
equations.justification: The abstract gives the inner-product interpretation; the explicit sum form is the standard definition and is inferred.
assumptions: Vectors a and b have equal finite length

registers.name: x
registers.role: Data register holding the input x in the computational basis, transformed by QFT and returned to the computational basis as x+a mod N

registers.name: ctrl
registers.role: Assumed control qubit for the controlled weighted sum variant; not specified by the abstract

specification.initial_state: |x> on the n-qubit data register with x in {0,...,N-1}, and the control qubit in |+> for the controlled variant (assumed)

steps.description: Apply QFT to the data register to move |x> into the Fourier basis.
Apply Fourier-domain phase rotations parameterized by the addend a, which add a modulo N in the transform domain.
Apply inverse QFT to return the register to the computational basis, yielding |x+a mod N>.

For the weighted average, accumulate weighted phase contributions w_i x_i in the transform domain and target the normalized sum given by the weighted average formula; the exact accumulation circuit is not specified by the abstract.

For the controlled weighted sum, condition the accumulation on the control qubit so the resulting sum corresponds to the inner product of the two data vectors; the exact encoding is not specified by the abstract.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the data register after the inverse QFT, repeated over shots to estimate the output distribution; the exact measurement protocol for the weighted average and inner product is not specified by the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical postprocessing would convert measured outcomes into the estimated modular sum and, for the weighted average, divide by the sum of weights; the exact estimator and its normalization are not specified by the abstract.
